rapport_notes: Warm, friendly tone throughout; good pacing and active listening; customer felt comfortable sharing details.
process_discipline_notes: No repetitions detected; no silence violations (customer cut call short naturally).

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep launches straight into 'reaching out I got your message. You've kind of like, there's gonna be like a corporate move' — no time-boxed ask or framing of benefit in return.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep moves immediately into logistics probing: 'it was a one bedroom apartment. And then as far as like packing there's gonna be like kind of dishes.'
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no concerns raised by customer that would require follow-up; customer responded to logistics questions with straightforward answers.
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with: Never mentioned. No 'what do you need us to be careful with' question.
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: Never mentioned. No 'who's actually showing up' or Meet Your Mover framing.
evidence_quotes.communication: Never mentioned. No day-before call, crew lead name, or inbox updates discussed.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: 'A one bedroom apartment move typically takes two guys around two and a half to three and a half hours and then packing usually takes about the same but I would put your packing. More along the line so like an hour and a half maybe so to do a pack and move for this, I would probably put you maybe in the range of about four to five hours.' — gives range and personalizes to their minimal packing.
evidence_quotes.beats_it_pay_less: 'Once we exceed the minimum we bill in fifteen minute increments until the move is completed so you just pay for the time use.' — implies they only pay for time used, but not explicit 'if crew beats it, you pay less' framing.
evidence_quotes.close_rate_lock: Not mentioned. Rep does not say 'your rate locks when you book.'
evidence_quotes.close_explicit_ask: Rep says 'I'll let you go now but yeah, I'll send over this email' and later 'if anything comes up questions wise feel free to email' — no direct ask for booking or commitment. Customer asks about 30th availability as a contingency, but rep never closes with 'would you like our help' or equivalent booking ask.

top_strength: Excellent logistics probing and pricing explanation — rep clearly laid out the hourly rate, minimum, 15-minute increments, supply costs, and time estimate in a way the customer understood and accepted without pushback.
coaching_note: Never asked for the customer's agenda or concerns before diving into logistics; skip all four differentiators (damage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time, Communication) and close without an explicit booking ask — treat discovery and takeaway as mandatory, and always close with a rate-lock + clear 'shall we book' request.
